Interface RmiConnectionService

All Superinterfaces:
Remote
All Known Implementing Classes:
RmiConnectionEntryPoint
public interface RmiConnectionService extends Remote
Remote entry point published by the server in the RMI registry.

This interface represents only the first step of an RMI client connection. The client looks up an implementation of this service from the registry, passes its own RmiClientService callback, and receives a dedicated RmiServerService session in return.

The concrete server-side implementation is RmiConnectionEntryPoint. It creates one VirtualViewRMI per connected client. This keeps the registry object stateless and gives each client its own remote session, session id, and callback reference.

This split mirrors the TCP architecture:

  • TCP accepts a socket and creates one virtual view for that client;
  • RMI accepts a callback and returns one remote session for that client.

  • Method Details

    • connect

      RmiServerService connect(RmiClientService clientCallback) throws RemoteException
      Creates a new server-side RMI session for one client.

      The clientCallback parameter is the remote object exported by the client. The server stores it in the new session and uses it later to send server-to-client messages and keep-alive pings.

      Parameters:
      clientCallback - client-side callback used by the server to push messages back to this client
      Returns:
      dedicated remote server session used by the client to send commands after connection setup
      Throws:
      RemoteException - if the session cannot be created or the remote call fails
